cards.headline: Iran-linked attacks strike Bahrain and civilian facility

pages.text: Bahrain reported that Iranian-linked attacks on November 21, 2026, injured two people and caused a fire at a civilian industrial facility. The Bahraini government stated its air defense intercepted several Iranian attacks, which it described as a “heinous Iranian aggression.” Local sources in Bahrain reported loud explosions, and videos showed smoke rising from an unidentified location. Following the incident, Saudi Arabia's Foreign Ministry condemned the attacks on the civilian industrial facility and expressed full solidarity with Manama, supporting all measures Bahrain takes to protect its security and stability. Kuwait and Qatar also issued statements condemning the attacks. Qatar's Foreign Ministry characterized the attack as a “flagrant violation of its sovereignty and territorial integrity” and a breach of international law and the United Nations Charter. Simultaneously, reports emerged from southern Iran of explosions in Sirik.

Iran's semi-official Fars news agency reported that the Iranian military launched two waves of drone and ballistic missile attacks on the night of November 21, 2026, targeting four US bases in Bahrain, including Sheikh Isa and Juffair. The Iranian Revolutionary Guards Corps (IRGC) claimed it struck two Patriot defense batteries and a radar system. Bahrain and the US military did not confirm these specific claims. The attacks occurred as the US military has regularly retaliated against Iranian military facilities in recent weeks. In response to potential US engagement of an Iranian convoy, Iran warned of a “fierce military response” and threatened widespread attacks on energy infrastructures across the Gulf region. Iranian deputy foreign minister Gharibabadi announced that Tehran has warned the United States that the Iranian convoy will soon sail to China.

Diplomatic efforts continue amid the crisis. On November 20, 2026, a Qatari delegation held talks with Iranian officials for approximately two hours before returning to Doha. Iranian Foreign minister Abbas Araghchi suggested a deal is possible if the US accepts Iran's “reasonable conditions,” such as ending the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, lifting sanctions, and acknowledging “past mistakes.” On November 21, 2026, US president Donald Trump told Fox News he intends to reach a “permanent” deal with Iran to prevent it from acquiring nuclear weapons, stating he is not interested in regime change in Iran. The Washington-based Institute for the Study of War noted that Iranian attempts to run the blockade present the United States with dilemmas regarding either collapsing the blockade or returning to a war that could strain relationships with Gulf allies.

pages.text: A nationwide Russian assault involving ballistic missiles left at least nine people dead, according to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, who described the attack as one of the most massive strikes of the war so far. The strikes targeted railway stations and key crossings in Kyiv, including bridges, during an overnight attack. This escalation follows recent damage caused by Ukraine to the strategically important Crimean Bridge, a structure built by the Kremlin to connect Russia to the occupied Crimean peninsula. Russian President Vladimir Putin had previously threatened to retaliate for the damage to that bridge.

cards.headline: Four dead and 162 injured in violent supercell storm in Tupancireta, Brazil

pages.text: A violent supercell storm tore through the agricultural town of Tupancireta in Rio Grande do Sul state, Brazil, killing four people and injuring 162. Civil defense authorities classified the storm as a supercell, a powerful thunderstorm characterized by strong rising air currents that can produce tornadoes. The storm struck the town in approximately 40 minutes before dawn, leaving residents without electricity or running water. According to Brazil’s national meteorological institute, Inmet, winds reached 114 kilometers (71 miles) per hour during the event. One person who was hospitalized died, bringing the total death toll to four, while the number of injured people increased from an earlier tally of 60 to 162, according to civil defense authorities.

The storm caused extensive structural damage, tearing roofs from thousands of buildings and damaging approximately 8,000 homes, as well as schools and the local hospital. Aerial images captured by AFP showed roofless houses and sheds stretching for kilometers, with debris and fallen trees littering the streets. Mayor Gustavo Herter said, “The town is gone.” The destruction included thousands of fallen electricity poles. Almost all of the town’s roughly 20,000 residents were forced to leave their homes, though only around 30 sought refuge in public shelters.

In the aftermath, residents have been salvaging furniture, mattresses, and bicycles from the wreckage or performing makeshift repairs on rooftops. Ivair Prieto, a 64-year-old bricklayer, told AFP that his house had been torn apart, stating, “We lost everything, we lost everything. But nobody was hurt, and life goes on,” as he pointed to the ruins of his home. Tupancireta is located nearly 400 kilometers (250 miles) inland from Porto Alegre on the coast.

cards.headline: Violence spreads across 28 districts in Bangladesh following protests over Sheikh Hasina's planned return

pages.text: Bangladesh has deployed paramilitary troops to contain a wave of violence that has erupted across 28 districts since mid-November. The unrest followed protests by supporters of former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, who are demonstrating against the government's rejection of her planned return to the country. At least four people have been killed during a week of violence that included attacks on banks, police stations, and the ancestral home of Nobel Peace Prize winner and former interim leader Muhammad Yunus.

The conflict centers on the status of Sheikh Hasina, who has been living in self-imposed exile in India since fleeing Bangladesh during a student-led uprising in July 2024. Hasina has requested a new identity card and passport to facilitate her return, but the current government, led by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, maintains she is a convicted criminal. The government stated she can only return under an extradition treaty with India. Hasina was previously sentenced to death in absentia by Bangladesh’s International Crimes Tribunal for crimes against humanity related to the 2024 student-led protests.

The protests, led by supporters of the now-banned Awami League party, overlapped with the anniversary of Hasina's death sentence. On November 20, 2026, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman addressed parliament, blaming India for the unrest. Rahman stated that those who fled to the country across the border have been conspiring against the interests of Bangladesh and its people to satisfy their masters.

cards.headline: Libya loses more than $30.8 million as armed group blocks oil pipeline for more than 20 days

pages.text: Libya has lost more than $30.8 million in oil revenue after an armed group forcibly shut the Hamada oil pipeline for more than 20 days, according to the National Oil Corporation (NOC). The shutdown disrupted the transportation of 302,778 barrels of crude, valued at $30.79 million based on average crude prices. The NOC stated that the losses also include fixed operating costs at affected Arabian Gulf Oil Company fields, including Hamada, NC5, NC8, and Tahara (NC4). During the disruption, crude output was reduced by an average of 14,418 barrels per day, resulting in daily revenue losses of approximately $1.47 million.

The Hamada pipeline serves as a key link in Libya’s oil transportation network, connecting the Hamada oilfields to the Zawiya refinery. The Zawiya refinery is the country's largest facility, with a processing capacity of 120,000 barrels per day, and is connected to the Sharara oilfield, which has a production capacity of about 300,000 barrels per day. On Oct. 31, an armed group shut a valve on the main Hamada crude pipeline, halting flows to Zawiya and marking the second interruption of oil supplies to the refinery that month. At that time, the NOC warned the closure could result in the loss of about 15,000 barrels of crude daily and urged the Petroleum Facilities Guard, which is responsible for securing oil installations, to help reopen the valve.

The NOC condemned attacks on oil infrastructure, stating they cause material and reputational damage to Libya’s energy sector. The corporation warned that these disruptions undermine efforts to increase production capacity and restore the confidence of international energy companies. Additionally, the NOC said the disruptions damage the country’s economy, hinder development efforts, and threaten the operation of state institutions. The corporation has called on relevant authorities to intensify efforts to reopen the pipeline valve and prevent further attacks to safeguard national resources.

cards.headline: Death outside Port Hardy Hospital raises concerns over rural emergency care access

pages.text: The death of a woman on the grounds of Port Hardy Hospital on northern Vancouver Island has renewed scrutiny regarding emergency medical access in rural British Columbia. The incident occurred on Nov. 19, just minutes after the hospital's emergency department had reached its scheduled 5 p.m. closing time. A paramedic from B.C. Emergency Health Services (BCEHS) became aware of a patient needing medical treatment in the parking lot at 5:11 p.m. Two additional ambulances responded, and paramedics provided emergency treatment before transferring the patient to hospital staff in critical condition. Island Health confirmed that both its healthcare providers and BCEHS paramedics responded and provided emergency interventions. Officials have not confirmed how long the patient was outside the hospital or what led to the medical emergency. Island Health stated it is reviewing the circumstances of the case and noted it would be inappropriate to speculate on contributing factors while the review is underway. The health authority has not confirmed whether the person sought care before the emergency response or if anyone was denied medical attention.

The emergency department at Port Hardy Hospital has closed daily at 5 p.m. since early 2023 due to staffing shortages, leaving the northern Vancouver Island community without 24/7 emergency services. North Island MLA and B.C. Minister of State for Rural Development Anna Kindy identified the deceased as a woman in a Facebook statement expressing condolences. While Kindy noted that emergency staff were available to respond in this specific case, she acknowledged that many rural communities like Port Hardy lack 24/7 emergency care. Dr. Alex Nataros, a family physician and founder of the North Island Community Health Centre, said some residents live in anxiety or fear after 5 p.m. when the emergency room closes. Nataros noted that patients may be older, have complex chronic diseases, or may be unable to drive the 43 kilometres to Port McNeill, which can be a difficult and icy road. Nataros stated his understanding, via a physician colleague involved in resuscitation efforts, is that the patient had been outside for an extended period before being brought into the emergency department. He reported his colleague performed an intraosseous procedure, which involves accessing bone marrow to administer emergency medications when conventional intravenous access cannot be quickly established.

cards.headline: Cartel leader Fausto Isidro Meza Flores captured in Sinaloa, Mexico, after firefight leaves at least 11 dead

pages.text: Mexican authorities captured cartel boss Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as “El Chapo Isidro,” during an overnight operation in Sinaloa state that left at least 11 people dead. The operation, which involved heavy gunfire, helicopters, and burning trucks, terrorized residents of the city of Guasave. Following his capture, Meza Flores was flown to Mexico City. The Mexican Defense Ministry reported that the firefight between Mexican forces and cartel gunmen killed seven alleged cartel gunmen and four Mexican soldiers. Authorities in the United States and Mexico celebrated the arrest as a security win. Meza Flores was one of the FBI's 10 most wanted fugitives and was wanted for illegally carrying firearms and trafficking drugs to the U.S. The United States had offered a $5 million reward for information leading to his arrest.

Meza Flores previously rose through the cartel ranks to lead the Beltrán Leyva cartel before becoming the leader of the Meza-Flores Transnational Criminal Organization. He was also a key ally to “Los Mayos,” a faction of the Sinaloa Cartel that the Trump administration designated as a foreign terrorist organization. His capture occurs as the cartel fights with another faction for control of the northern Mexican state. The Mexican government stated in a report that intelligence from the Trump administration helped authorities capture Meza Flores, though the report provided few details regarding how Mexican and United States authorities coordinated the detention.

cards.headline: First unit of Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant begins trial electricity supply to Bangladesh national grid

pages.text: The first unit of the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant in Pabna, Bangladesh, began feeding electricity into the national grid on a trial basis on November 20, 2026. The first grid synchronisation occurred at 3:16pm, nearly nine years after construction of the Tk 1.39 lakh crore project began. Science and Technology Minister Fakir Mahbub Anam, who was present at the plant, described the event as a “historic achievement.” While the electricity generated during this testing period can be used by consumers, an uninterrupted supply cannot yet be guaranteed. The development does not mean the plant has entered commercial operation; Unit 1 must undergo several rounds of technical tests and regulatory checks before it can supply electricity commercially at full capacity.

According to the science and technology ministry, the unit initially supplied up to 350 megawatts (MW) before its output was reduced to 300MW to maintain grid stability. Project Director Md Kabir Hossain stated that the initial grid connection would last approximately eight to 10 hours, after which the unit would be disconnected for further tests. The unit is expected to be reconnected after a break of about 28 hours, initially supplying electricity for four to six hours. These tests are designed to assess the performance of the turbine, generator, control systems, and the equipment connecting the plant to the national grid. During this process, output may be raised or lowered, and the unit may be temporarily disconnected as required.

cards.headline: At least three dead and 36 missing after fire at Indonesian confectionery factory

pages.text: A fire at the Fonusa Agung Mulia confectionery factory in Cikande, Indonesia, has killed three people and left 36 others missing, according to search and rescue official Rizky Dwianto. Banten province governor Andra Soni told reporters that an estimated 60 people were inside the facility when the fire broke out on the afternoon of November 21, 2026. Four people were injured and transported to a nearby hospital and health clinic.

Fire official Tubagus Machfudz told local broadcaster Kompas TV that firefighters were alerted at approximately 4:30pm on November 21, 2026, and found the building already engulfed in flames upon arrival. Machfudz stated that because a large area was already on fire, officials could not determine if the company’s protection system was functioning properly. cards.headline: Houses and shops attacked in Narail's Bendarchar village following deaths of two BNP leaders

pages.text: In Bendarchar village within the Kalia upazila of Narail, Bangladesh, several houses and shops belonging to Awami League leaders and activists were attacked, vandalized, looted, and set on fire on November 20, 2026. The violence followed the November 18, 2026, deaths of two Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) associate organization leaders, Sohail Rana, general secretary of the Kalia Upazila Bangladesh Jatiyatabadi Samajik Sangskritik Sangstha (JASAS), and Shahinur Islam, general secretary of the Municipal Krishak Dal, who were killed during an attack on a BNP motorcycle rally by Awami League activists. While the administration is investigating the identity of those responsible, Kalia Upazila Nirbahi Officer (UNO) Md Jinnatul Islam confirmed that several houses, including that of former MP BM Kabirul Haque, were attacked and 15-20 rooms were vandalized before dusk on November 20, 2026. Five to six rooms were set on fire, though no casualties were reported from these specific attacks.

Conflicting accounts exist regarding the scale and nature of the violence in Bendarchar. Residents of the village claimed that on the afternoon of November 20, 2026, BNP supporters attacked the homes of Awami League leaders, including BM Kabirul Haque Mukti and former municipal mayor Mushfiqur Rahman, resulting in approximately 50 houses and shops being vandalized, looted, and burned. Firefighters reported seeing 20 to 30 houses on fire when they arrived at the scene. However, Kalia Upazila BNP General Secretary SM Wahiduzzaman denied the allegations, calling the claims of arson and house attacks baseless and stating that the idea that these acts occurred in the presence of BNP leaders is fictional. He also disputed social media reports claiming over 200 homes were attacked. Narail District Police issued a press release stating that reports of attacks on Hindu homes in Bendarchar are false and fabricated, noting there is no Hindu settlement in the area and that Awami League activists have shared misrepresenting videos on social media. The police noted that around 4:45 pm on November 20, 2026, relatives of the deceased BNP leaders gathered in the village and attacked the houses of Awami League activists they believed were involved in the murders.

cards.headline: Researchers use quantum physics to verify physical location in lab experiment

pages.text: Physicists led by the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) have conducted a first-of-its-kind experiment using quantum physics to confirm a person's location. Described in the journal Nature on November 18, 2026, the experiment involved researchers verifying a location by having a participant catch a single photon fired at them through a fiber-optic cable using some-second timing. This method offers a potential new defense against digital imposters who may spoof identities, passwords, or security camera footage to hide their true physical whereabouts.

cards.headline: Children in Gaza struggle to access life-saving insulin

pages.text: Families in the Gaza Strip are struggling to obtain insulin and blood glucose testing supplies, forcing them to make difficult choices to keep children alive. In Gaza City, nine-year-old Amir was admitted to intensive care after experiencing severe abdominal pain and vomiting. Doctors found a dangerous build-up of acid in his blood caused by insulin poisoning, according to his mother, Nahawand. Amir was diagnosed with type 1 diabetes at one year old, a condition requiring constant blood sugar monitoring and insulin adjustments based on meals and readings.

The cost of insulin has risen significantly due to Israel’s siege on Gaza and local economic factors, such as Nahawand's husband being out of work. Before the war, a single insulin pen cost between 25 and 30 shekels ($7.62 to $9.17) or was provided for free through aid organisations and clinics. Currently, a pen costs between 50 and 80 shekels ($15.29 to $24.46). Nahawand told Al Jazeera that she is unable to afford insulin for her son. After months of searching for supplies in Gaza City, she obtained medicine brought from Khan Younis in southern Gaza, only to find the supplies had expired.

cards.headline: Teenager and mother assist in rescue of missing 17-year-old girl

pages.text: Landon Tresp, 16, and his mother, Khristina, 41, helped facilitate the rescue of a 17-year-old girl who had been missing for more than a year. The rescue occurred 24 hours after Landon alerted his mother to the girl's situation. The girl, whose identity the BBC is protecting, told Landon she was being held against her will hundreds of miles from home, though she did not know her exact location. She was 15 when she first went missing. The Tresps provided the BBC with screenshots of communication and a photo matching a criminal complaint to corroborate their account.

Landon Tresp met the girl while playing the online game Among Us at his family's Colorado mountain home. After approximately two weeks of chatting, Landon informed Khristina, a nurse and mother of five, about the situation on 31 October. Following this briefing, the mother and son worked to track the girl, contact her mother, and cooperate with the FBI. During a call with Khristina, the girl reportedly showed her a knife that her alleged captor kept under his pillow.

cards.headline: Bangladesh Ministry of Finance drafts amendments to Bank Company Act to curb political and family influence

pages.text: The Bangladesh Ministry of Finance has finalized a draft of amendments to the Bank Company Act, 1991, intended to reduce political and family influence in the banking sector, strengthen the recovery of defaulted loans, and protect depositors' interests. The proposed changes aim to establish better governance within the industry through stricter rules on board composition and leadership roles. Under the draft, cabinet members or officials of equivalent rank, members of parliament, and local government representatives would be barred from serving as directors, managing directors, or chief executive officers of banks. This would be in addition to existing disqualifications for individuals with criminal convictions, financial offenses, regulatory breaches, loan defaults, or those lacking at least 10 years of relevant experience. Dr. Zaidi Sattar, Chairman of the Policy Research Institute of Bangladesh (PRI), welcomed the proposed bars on politicians and public representatives, noting that long tenures risk excessive influence and insider lending. He stated that strong legal measures are necessary to prevent past plundering and assist in economic recovery.

The draft proposes several changes to limit family dominance over bank management and ownership. If enacted, the maximum number of members from a single family allowed on a bank's board of directors would decrease from three to two. Additionally, representation on a board by entities owned or controlled by the same family would be reduced from a maximum of two to one. The amendments also seek to halve the maximum continuous tenure for a director from 12 years to six years. This six-year cap would be followed by a three-year cooling-off period, and any periods of service under three years would still count toward the six-year limit. To increase oversight, the draft proposes increasing the number of independent directors: boards with 20 directors would require at least four independent directors instead of three, while boards with fewer than 20 would require at least three instead of two. The definition of an independent director would be updated to exclude anyone with at least three years of past affiliation or interest tied to the bank or its related parties. Finally, while the 10 per cent single or joint shareholding cap for individuals, companies, or families remains, the draft proposes empowering Bangladesh Bank to relax this cap for strategic investors based on central bank criteria and sector interests.

cards.headline: Researchers identify genetic eye disease that causes loss of night vision and peripheral sight

pages.text: An international research team has identified a new genetic eye disease that gradually impairs night vision and the ability to see objects at the edges of a person's visual field. Researchers are calling the condition EFEMP1-associated late-onset retinal degeneration (L-ORD), though it has not yet received an official name. The disease may be difficult to detect because individuals can maintain good eyesight for much of their lives before noticeable vision problems develop. The study, published in JAMA Ophthalmology, traces the investigation back to 1998 when doctors documented an unusual pattern of vision loss in a family in the United States. As new genetic evidence emerged, researchers connected those findings to families in Europe exhibiting similar symptoms.

The condition is linked to a specific genetic variant known as p.Arg140Trp in the EFEMP1 gene. This genetic change causes an unusually thick accumulation of material to build up between cells in the eye. While the EFEMP1 gene is already associated with another form of vision loss, the two diseases affect eyesight in different ways. The previously known disorder primarily damages central vision, whereas the newly discovered L-ORD affects peripheral vision and the ability to see in darkness. In the study, researchers compared the symptoms of three unrelated families from different countries carrying the p.Arg140Trp variant against another family carrying a different change in the same gene, called p.Arg345Trp, which is associated with the known central vision disorder. The research included scientists from the Scheie Eye Institute within the University of Pennsylvania's Perelman School of Medicine.

cards.headline: Garment workers stage protests in Gazipur, Savar, Ashulia, and Mirpur

pages.text: Garment workers staged fresh protests in Gazipur, Savar, Ashulia, and Mirpur on November 22, 2026, amid ongoing labour unrest over wage-related demands. In Gazipur, police used at least five sound grenades to disperse workers who were blocking roads, while in Savar, police used tear gas shells and sound grenades to disperse protesters. The unrest led to chases between workers and law enforcers in Gazipur and prompted several factories to announce closures one after another. In Gazipur's Bhogra, workers began protesting in front of the Euro Jeans factory around 8:30am. By approximately 9:15am, workers had broken a section of the road divider on the Bhogra-Tangail road and placed it across the carriageway to halt traffic. Traffic Inspector Tarikul Islam reported that labour unrest was continuing in Bhogra, where hundreds of workers took positions on both sides of the road between Bhogra and Nawjor in solidarity with the protesters. cards.headline: Diplomats struggle to reach fossil fuel agreement at Cop31 in Turkey

pages.text: Negotiators at the Cop31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, are facing deep divisions after a revised draft deal released on November 19, 2026, removed all mentions of fossil fuels. The removal of these references has forced representatives from nearly 200 countries back to the bargaining table as they attempt to secure a final agreement. The European Union stated that the revised draft risked turning the summit into a fossil fuel summit. On November 20, 2026, nations including France and Panama issued a letter insisting that the final deal must include a clear transition away from fossil fuels. Panama's environment minister, Juan Carlos Navarro, accused a petroleum mafia of blocking progress and threatened to walk away from the talks. COP31 President and Turkish Environment Minister Murat Kurum told an assembly late on November 20, 2026, that while negotiators are close to the finish line, they have not yet reached it. Australian Climate Minister Chris Bowen, who is leading negotiations, said he would work for as long as it takes to complete the task.

While climate negotiations in Turkey faced deadlock, a separate fuel deal was struck in Shenzhen, China, on November 19, 2026, between the US, China, and Russia to boost oil production. Matt Webb, a diplomacy expert at the climate thinktank E3G, described the deal on November 21, 2026, as another symptom of a global crisis driven by continued dependence on volatile fossil fuels. Webb noted that US refineries are currently at 95% to 96% utilisation. He stated that Washington is essentially asking Beijing to mobilise its estimated 4.8 to 5.1m barrels per day of spare capacity to offset the strait of Hormuz shock. This conflict, according to the IEA’s World Energy Outlook 2026, cut global supply by 16.1m barrels per day at its peak and is described as the largest energy supply shock in history. Separately, OPEC Secretary General Haitham al-Ghais met with Russian climate envoy Ruslan Edelgeriev at Cop31 to discuss enhancing cooperation between OPEC and the Russian Federation regarding international climate action and sustainable development.

cards.headline: Navdeep Bains elected leader of Ontario Liberal Party

pages.text: Navdeep Bains has been elected as the new leader of the Ontario Liberal Party following a nine-month leadership race. Bains secured 50.3 per cent of the vote on the third and final ballot at a leadership convention in downtown Toronto, defeating the next closest competitor, provincial caucus member Lee Fairclough, who received 49.7 per cent of the vote. The narrow margin placed Bains less than one percentage point ahead of Fairclough during the announcement to a crowd of more than 1,000 Liberals at the Metro Toronto Convention Centre. Bains, a former federal cabinet minister in Justin Trudeau’s government and former industry minister, previously served five terms federally in the Greater Toronto areas of Mississauga and Brampton before leaving a role as chief corporate affairs officer at Rogers Communications earlier this spring to return to politics.

The Ontario Liberal Party has been without a long-term leader since the resignation of Bonnie Crombie in January. Bains is expected to lead the party into the next provincial election, which may not occur until 2030. Following the results, Bains stated that the end of the leadership race is the beginning of a campaign to replace Doug Ford and the Progressive Conservative Party of Ontario. Premier Doug Ford congratulated Bains on social media platform X, stating that Ontario families are counting on the party to work collaboratively to address tariffs, protect workers, and make life more affordable. The provincial Liberal party aims to rebuild after three consecutive election losses to present an alternative to the Progressive Conservatives.

Bains faces the challenge of leading the party without currently holding a seat in the Ontario legislature. This marks the third time since 2020 that party members have selected a leader who does not hold a seat in the legislature. During the race, some members suggested the party should select a leader who already has a voice in Queen's Park, the provincial legislature. Bains told reporters at a media availability that he will be seeking a seat, though he did not specify a location or timing for his candidacy. He noted that he would not ask any of the current 14 Members of Provincial Parliament (MPPs) to resign to facilitate his run. Other contenders in the leadership race included Stephanie Bowman, a former finance executive and two-term MPP from Toronto, and Dylan Marando, a former senior adviser in federal and provincial Liberal governments.

cards.headline: Surgeons at Korle Bu Teaching Hospital in Ghana reattach man's severed penis

pages.text: Specialists at the Urology and Nephrology Centre of the Korle Bu Teaching Hospital in Ghana have successfully reattached a man's severed penis following a rare and complex surgical procedure. The hospital's Board Chair, Professor Titus Beyuo, disclosed the achievement during an appearance on Accra-based Channel One TV on Saturday, November 21, 2026. According to Professor Beyuo, the surgical team successfully reattached the organ and restored its function.

The injury occurred after the patient reportedly slipped while attempting to sit on a water closet (WC), which resulted in the severing of his penis. Professor Beyuo described the successful operation as a significant medical achievement for the hospital's specialists.

cards.headline: New imaging technique maps large volumes of brain tissue in nanoscale detail

pages.text: Researchers at Harvard Medical School and the University of California San Diego have developed a method to speed up imaging techniques, allowing them to map large volumes of brain tissue in nanoscale detail for the first time. This advancement enables scientists to create more complete connectomes, which are diagrams used by neuroscientists to understand how neurons connect to produce thought and behavior. By revealing fine structures that previous maps could miss, the technique may deepen understanding of nervous-system development and various brain diseases. The work was described in the journal Nature Methods. According to Wei-Chung Allen Lee, an associate professor of neurobiology at Harvard Medical School and an associate professor of neurology at Boston Children's Hospital, the method allows researchers to see brain structures previously invisible in connectomics data. Lee stated that the work aims to help scientists understand how nervous systems are built, how they change with age, and what causes issues in neurodevelopmental, cognitive, and neurodegenerative disorders.

cards.headline: Restored wells provide water to households in Hebron’s Old City

pages.text: The Hebron Rehabilitation Committee has restored 108 abandoned wells in the Old City of Hebron, in the occupied West Bank, to address chronic water shortages. The project aims to provide families with a reliable source of clean water by restoring neglected wells located on private properties. The committee launched the initiative in July after monitoring water shortages for two years, inviting residents to register wells on their land. More than 70 households registered in the first few days of the campaign, and approximately 215 have registered since. The committee intends to complete work on the remaining registered wells.

Water shortages in the Old City of Hebron have created hardships that threaten the Palestinian identity of the historic area. Residents face difficulties with daily tasks such as cleaning and preparing meals due to limited access to water. Municipal water reaches some homes only once a month, and many families lack the storage capacity to maintain supplies between deliveries. Water tankers also struggle to reach Palestinian homes because of the area's narrow streets and the presence of numerous military gates and checkpoints. Additionally, settlers occupying the rooftops of Palestinian shops and homes make it difficult for locals to install water tanks to mitigate the crisis.

cards.headline: Chemical signatures suggest babies in ancient Greek colony Himera started solid foods at 3 months but nursed for nearly 4 years

pages.text: A study published in the European Journal of Archaeology indicates that infants in the ancient Greek colony of Himera began eating solid foods at approximately 3 months of age but were not fully weaned until around 3.8 years old. Researchers reached these findings by analyzing chemical signatures in the bones of children from the site, which was an ancient Greek outpost located in Sicily between the seventh and fifth centuries B.C. This timeline of weaning is much longer than what ancient writers had previously suggested. Himera was founded by Dorian and Chalcidian colonists and grew into a large city with a multicultural population that included Greeks, Phoenicians, and local Sicilians.

Archaeologists have uncovered over 13,000 burials at the site, many of which are adults. The study reported that infant and child mortality appeared to be surprisingly low. Laurie Reitsema, a biological anthropologist at the University of Georgia, described the findings as evidence of mothers' responsiveness to infant needs 2,500 years ago. The study noted that while the population was culturally diverse, the practice of beginning weaning early and continuing it for a long duration was shared across these different backgrounds. The researchers suggested that children born into this diverse environment likely experienced different cultural realities than their parents, potentially serving as seeds for cultural change across generations.

cards.headline: Women farmers in Ghana increase maize yields by 140% through agroecology

pages.text: Women farmers in Ghana's Bono, Bono East, and Ahafo regions have increased maize yields by 140% by adopting agroecological farming, though many still face barriers to land ownership and credit. Agroecology is a farming method that relies on materials already available on a farm—such as manure, mulch, and crop diversity—instead of purchasing chemical inputs. Since 2016, ActionAid Ghana has worked with smallholder women farmers in these regions to build skills in these techniques, training more than 700 women and establishing three community seed banks to preserve indigenous crop varieties.

Diana Afriyie, a farmer in the Smallholder Women Farmers Movement (SHWFM), reported that her maize harvest on a four-acre farm increased from 20 bags to 48 bags per season after switching to organic, nature-based farming. Previously, Afriyie spent thousands of Ghana cedis each season to buy approximately 15 bags of chemical fertiliser. She has since replaced those inputs with manure from her own poultry farm, diversified her crops, and stopped burning her farm after weeding to help retain soil moisture during dry spells. Another SHWFM farmer, Selina Asante, has utilized crop rotation and mulching to prevent crops from drying out during extended periods without rain.

Despite these productivity gains, women in the three regions struggle to expand their farming operations due to limited access to irrigation, credit, and land. Clementina Ayivor, President of the Ahafo Regional SHWFM, stated that land ownership and control in many communities remain with men, including husbands, family heads, and traditional authorities. This leaves women dependent on others for farmland access, which prevents them from making long-term investments or deciding how much land to cultivate. To address financial hurdles, ActionAid has supported women in forming or strengthening village savings and loan associations to increase access to farming funds.
